summary: The Type-I slice (CONDITIONAL_ES Lemma 1.1, parameter t) gives a concrete witness: first witness t_min for primes p≡1 (mod 4) has median 3 over 39,175 primes ≤ 10⁶, so the typical first witness is found by factoring tp+1 ≈ 3p, an integer of size p. The divisor search 'divisor of tp+1 in class −1 mod t' is therefore a factorisation-type problem at small t, and only the Lenstra/Hales regime (t³ > tp+1, i.e. t ≳ √p) is known to be polynomial. The cost of factoring p-size numbers is what a witness search at small t pays.
not_done: No timing at p ~ 10^30; the claim "as hard as factoring" is not established, only that the first witness is typically a factorisation of a ~p-size number.

summary: Classified all sorted 3-term solutions of 4/m² for odd m ≤ 61 by the number of denominators divisible by m.
